feat(beadrs-3ab387b2): skip publication when the checkpoint covers the live sequence

The post-commit chokepoint now treats an advanced sequence as necessary
but not sufficient: publication is also skipped when the pointer's
snapshot_sequence already covers the live event sequence (plan 6.2.1
item 3), so a no-op mutation mints no generation and no object, and a
pointer another publisher already carried to this sequence or beyond --
the residue of a lost publication race -- is treated as success rather
than published over.

`sync flush-only` becomes idempotent to match (item 8): against a clean,
ready-to-commit checkpoint it publishes nothing, reports "already
current", and exits 0. The skip is bounded by readiness, not just
cleanliness -- a not-ready checkpoint with unresolved tombstones, the
state an interrupted cleanup leaves behind, still republishes and
reapplies the cleanup.

test_f017_identical_flushes_reuse_one_object pinned the superseded
clean-reflush-republishes behavior; its republication is now triggered
by a lost pointer (the state an interrupted publication actually leaves,
since current.json commits last), preserving every object-reuse
assertion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
